vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: htpasswd
Version: 1.0.3

The skill is classified as suspicious due to a significant discrepancy between its stated purpose and its actual implementation. While SKILL.md and the metadata describe it as a security tool for managing Apache/Nginx htpasswd files (including password generation and verification), the code in scripts/script.sh is actually a generic text list manager that stores entries in plain text JSON format without any cryptographic hashing or standard htpasswd formatting. This misrepresentation could lead users to believe they are securing a system while actually storing credentials in plain text, although the script lacks explicit logic for data exfiltration or remote execution.

llm.summary: The package claims to be an htpasswd manager but the shipped script does not produce htpasswd-formatted hashes or perform verification and also omits declaring a dependency on python3; it will store arbitrary plaintext entries in a user data directory — review before use.

dimensions.detail: The skill advertises 'Generate htpasswd entries' and 'verify passwords' for Apache/Nginx, but the included script only stores arbitrary JSONL entries (field 'text') and provides CRUD/search/export over them; there is no code to create htpasswd-compatible salted hashes, no password verification routine, and no integration with Apache/Nginx configuration. This is a functional mismatch: it behaves like a generic entry store rather than an htpasswd generator/validator.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and the script operate only on a local data directory (default: ~/.local/share/htpasswd or HTPASSWD_DIR). The script reads/writes those files and a config.json; it also reads environment variables HTPASSWD_DIR, XDG_DATA_HOME, and HOME. No network calls, external endpoints, or other system files are accessed. Important: the code will store whatever you pass (including passwords) in plaintext JSONL.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (instruction-only) and no downloads. The only shipped code is a local script. This minimizes install-time risk because nothing is fetched from external URLs, but you should still review the included script before running it.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The manifest declares no required env vars, but the script expects HTPASSWD_DIR (optional) and implicitly uses XDG_DATA_HOME and HOME. More importantly, SKILL.md claims 'No external dependencies required' while the script invokes python3 repeatedly. The missing declaration of python3 as a dependency is an inconsistency to be aware of.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request elevated privileges or permanent platform-wide presence (always: false). It only creates/reads files inside the user-scoped data directory. It does not modify other skills or system-wide agent settings.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package is suspicious because its README and description promise htpasswd generation and password verification but the script stores arbitrary plaintext entries in a local JSONL file and lacks htpasswd-compatible hashing/verify logic. Before installing or using it: (1) review the script thoroughly; do not store real passwords with it as they will be saved in plaintext; (2) ensure python3 is present (the script uses python3 despite the manifest claiming no deps); (3) if you need real Apache/Nginx basic-auth files, prefer the system 'htpasswd' tool (from apache2-utils/htpasswd) or a tool that explicitly implements bcrypt/MD5/APR1 hashing; (4) consider modifying the script to perform proper password hashing/verification and to avoid storing sensitive secrets in plaintext, or run it only on throwaway data. If you cannot review or modify the script, treat it as untrusted for handling real credentials.
